summary.para: The D compiler to use. &SCons; provides tool modules for three D compilation systems: DMD (&t-link-dmd;), the reference compiler; LDC (&t-link-ldc;), the LLVM-based D compiler; and GDC (&t-link-gdc;), from the GNU Compiler Collection, searched in that order. Use a tool specifier if you need to prefer a specific compiler. See also &cv-link-SHDC; for compiling to shared objects.

The command line used to compile a D file to an object file. Any options specified in the &cv-link-DFLAGS; construction variable are included on this command line. See also &cv-link-SHDCOM; for compiling to shared objects. See also the &b-link-ProgramAllAtOnce; builder for how to compile directly to an executable without making intermediate object files.

If set, the string displayed when a D source file is compiled to an object file. If not set, then &cv-link-DCOM; (the command line) is displayed. See also &cv-link-SHDCOMSTR; for compiling to shared objects.
Debug tags to enable when compiling.
Prefix used for debug tags from &cv-link-DDEBUG;. Defaults vary by D compiler.
Suffix used for debug tags from &cv-link-DDEBUG;.
File suffix for D source files. The default is .d.
Prefix added to each element of &cv-link-DFLAGS;.
General options that are passed to the D compiler.
Suffix added to each element of &cv-link-DFLAGS;.
Suffix added to each path in &cv-link-DPATH;.
Prefix added to each path in &cv-link-DPATH;.
Name of the static library tool for D code.
The command line to use when linking a static library.
The flags to pass to the library tool.
The command-line prefix for library search directories from &cv-link-LIBPATH; when linking D code.
The command-line suffix for library search directories from &cv-link-LIBPATH; when linking D code.
Suffix added to each element of &cv-link-DLIBFLAGS;.
Prefix added to each element of &cv-link-DLIBFLAGS;.
Prefix added to each library name from &cv-link-LIBS;.
Suffix added to each library name from &cv-link-LIBS;.
Name of the linker to use for linking systems including D sources. See also &cv-link-SHDLINK; for linking shared objects.
The command line to use when linking systems including D sources. See also &cv-link-SHDLINKCOM; for linking shared objects.
Linker flags. See also &cv-link-SHDLINKFLAGS; for linking shared objects.
Suffix added to each element of &cv-link-DLINKFLAGS;.
Prefix added to each element of &cv-link-DLINKFLAGS;.
List of paths to search for import modules.
Prefix added to rpath entries when generating shared objects.
Suffix added to rpath entries when generating shared objects.
Prefix added to each element of &cv-link-DVERSIONS;.
List of version tags to enable when compiling.
Suffix added to each element of &cv-link-DVERSIONS;.
The name of the compiler to use when compiling D source destined to be in a shared object. See also &cv-link-DC; for compiling to static objects.
The command line to use when compiling code to be part of shared objects. See also &cv-link-DCOM; for compiling to static objects.

If set, the string displayed when a D source file is compiled to a (shared) object file. If not set, then &cv-link-SHDCOM; (the command line) is displayed. See also &cv-link-DCOMSTR; for compiling to static objects.
Extra flags added to &cv-link-SHDLINKCOM; when building versioned &b-link-SharedLibrary;. These flags are only used when &cv-link-SHLIBVERSION; is set.
The linker to use when creating shared objects from dlang code. See also &cv-link-DLINK; for linking static objects.
The command line to use when generating shared objects. See also &cv-link-DLINKCOM; for linking static objects.
The flags to use when generating a shared object for the D language. See also &cv-link-DLINKFLAGS; for linking static objects.
Suffix for D interface files, which are translations of C header files. The default is .di.
Path to search for D interface files, which are translations of C header files.
Prefix added to the name of the D interface file directory from &cv-link-DI_FILE_DIR;.
Suffix added to the name of the D interface file directory from &cv-link-DI_FILE_DIR;.
Builds an executable from D sources without first creating individual objects for each file.

D sources can be compiled file-by-file as C and C++ source are, and D is integrated into the &scons; &b-link-Object; and &b-link-Program; builders for this model of build. D codes can though do whole source meta-programming (some of the testing frameworks do this). For this it is imperative that all sources are compiled and linked in a single call to the D compiler. This builder serves that purpose.

This command will compile the modules mod_a, mod_b, and mod_c in a single compilation process without first creating object files for the modules. Some of the D compilers will create executable.o others will not.
